newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Forbes shares leap on listing.
newsitem.headline: Forbes shares leap on listing.

text.p: Shares in South African financial services group Forbes Ltd jumped on their first day's trading, dealers said on Monday.

The firm listed its shares at 535 cents each, but trading opened on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange at 700 cents and soon powered up to touch a high of 815 cents before slipping back to 800 at 0845 GMT.
"There has been heavy demand for the stock. It is seen as a great buy at its listing price," one dealer said.

Institutions in October eagerly snapped up a Forbes' tender offer to raise 60 million rand. The listing is expected to raise a total of 102.25 million rand which will be applied to developing the group's financial and professional services.
Forbes' two main businesses are employee benefits and actuarial consulting group Alexander Forbes, and risk management and insurance broking firm Price Forbes.
In its pre-listing statement Forbes said it expects attributable profit to rise 26 percent to 70 million in the year to March 31.
In the terms of the listing, shareholders in Servgro International Ltd, which owns 70 percent of Forbes, are being offered four new Forbes shares for every 100 Servgro shares held.
